verdicts.title: On the complete solution of the general quintic using Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this article we give solution of the general quintic equation by means of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction. More precisely we express a root of the quintic as a known algebraic function of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes solving general quintic equations via the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction, which shares only the 'continued fraction' vocabulary with the conjecture and has nothing to do with ACC⁰ circuit complexity or Boolean function restrictions.

verdicts.title: On a General Sextic Equation Solved by the Rogers Ramanujan Continued Fraction
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this article we solve a general class of sextic equations. The solution follows if we consider the $j$-invariant and relate it with the polynomial equation's coefficients. The form of the solution is a relation of Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction. The inverse technique can also be used for the evaluation of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction, in which the equation is not now the depressed equation but another quite more simplified equation.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns solving sextic equations via the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction and j-invariant, with no engagement with Boolean circuit complexity, ACC⁰ lower bounds, or greedy restriction trajectories.

verdicts.title: Continued fractions over non-Euclidean imaginary quadratic rings
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We propose and study a generalized continued fraction algorithm that can be executed in an arbitrary imaginary quadratic field, the novelty being a non-restriction to the five Euclidean cases. Many hallmark properties of classical continued fractions are shown to be retained, including exponential convergence, best-of-the-second-kind approximation quality (up to a constant), periodicity of quadratic irrational expansions, and polynomial time complexity.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a generalized continued fraction algorithm over imaginary quadratic rings, with no mention of Boolean functions, ACC⁰ circuits, or restriction-based bias trajectories — it shares only the 'continued fraction' vocabulary.
